decisions.issues: Minor only: the yard figures mostly face the house rather than clearly looking up at the wall, and the fort flies a plain white flag instead of the Travancore conch-on-red standard (the same white flag appears in panels 2, 4 and 5, so the page is consistent). Ridges, red earth, gold grass, village smoke, laterite wall behind bamboo scaffolding with masons, and the tiled house among pepper vines all match. No text, gore or anachronism. Large clear sky at upper left for both captions.

Nagoji's head is right: topknot, grey temples, gold ear stud, thick curled moustache, clean chin, silver chain and cream shoulder cloth. The trader is also right: short grey beard, checked lungi, striped towel and clay cup. But Nagoji's LEFT forearm has a dark ink tattoo shaped like a letter or glyph (about x 0.82, y 0.60). That is pseudo-text, and it contradicts the brand description (a pale puckered patch, no letters). There is also a white scar across the BACK of his left hand, where the bible forbids marks; the healed chapter 22 line belongs on the palm. Minor: the mundu falls to the ground instead of being hitched for riding.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition exactly: the grey-bearded trader seated on the verandah step at left in a blue-and-white checked lungi with a blue-striped towel over one shoulder, both hands around a clay cup, looking up and talking; Nagoji standing at right in the laterite fort courtyard with Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, small gold ear stud, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, silver chain of office, cream shoulder cloth, talwar at the hip, no turban, no red sash. Fix his LEFT arm: turn the left forearm so its inner side faces his thigh, hiding the old brand and the long scar, and draw NO tattoo, ink mark, glyph, letter, numeral, symbol or scar anywhere on the visible forearm or the back of the hand; the skin there is smooth and unmarked. The healed chapter 22 wound is only a thin pale line across the LEFT PALM, which faces his thigh and need not show. Hitch the white mundu up toward the knee for riding. No forehead mark. Keep the open sky above and between the two men clear for three balloons.

decisions.issues: Shrug, cup and hands are fine, but the trader no longer matches panel 1.2, the panel right before it. Here he wears a plain white mundu instead of the blue-and-white checked lungi, the striped towel over his shoulder is missing, and his beard is long and flowing instead of short and trimmed, so he reads as a different, older man. The framing is also not close: it runs down to his knees.
decisions.correction: This is the same trader as panel 1.2 and must match him exactly: a short, neatly trimmed grey beard close to the jaw (not long or flowing), short curly grey hair, bare-headed, bare-chested, a cream towel with blue stripes over one shoulder, and if any waist cloth shows it is a blue-and-white checked lungi, never a plain white mundu. Frame him close, cropped at mid-chest: head, shoulders and both hands fill the frame as he shrugs with one palm turned up and the clay cup of spiced buttermilk in the other hand, a wry sideways look. Keep the same shaded verandah posts, laterite courtyard wall and daylight as panel 1.2, with clear sky at the upper right for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Acceptable, with minor deviations: Ramayyan writes with a stylus on the palm-leaf bundle instead of tapping his fingers on it. Varma's hair knot sits low at the back of his head behind the near (right) ear rather than as a side knot above the left ear, though he is clearly bare-headed with no turban or crest. Varma looks off-panel to the right instead of straight at the reader, which still works spatially because the courtyard where Nagoji stood in panel 1.2 lies to the right of the verandah. Both faces match their sheets. Hands are sound. No text. The hanging brass lamp has an open wick. Clear sky at upper right, and a plain wall with roof beams at upper left, give room for both Ramayyan balloons.

Varma does not match the bible or panel 1.4. His hair hangs loose and wavy to the shoulders, with grey streaks at the temples, instead of sitting in a side knot above the left ear. He also has a white-and-red Vaishnavite namam on his brow, which panel 1.4 does not show and which the ch23 row does not call for. Loose curly hair, grey temples, curled moustache and gold earring together make him read like Nagoji, inviting confusion. The framing is waist-up rather than close.
decisions.correction: Match Varma to panel 1.4 on this page: the V13 sheet face, jet-black hair with NO grey anywhere, gathered into a neat side knot above his LEFT ear, with no loose hair falling to the neck or shoulders; a bare brow with no namam, tilak or forehead mark; curled moustache, pearl-drop gold earrings, gold bead necklaces, bare chest, cream mundu with a gold border over one shoulder, no turban, no crest, no bandage. Frame him close, head and shoulders only, in three-quarter view, eyes turned straight out of the panel toward the viewer (where Nagoji stands), one corner of the mouth lifting in the faintest edge of amusement. Keep the same laterite fort courtyard and verandah posts in dry daylight, with clear sky at the upper left for two balloons.

decisions.issues: v01 is otherwise strong: the column on red dirt, Nagoji (topknot, grey temples, gold ear stud, clean chin, thick curled moustache, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth) on an ochre-bay Kayal beside Padmini (grey-threaded hair, gold, cream sari, stick across the saddle), turbaned riders with tall spears, Nair matchlock men on foot, the light gun on a bullock-drawn carriage, and clear sky for both lettering lines. But Nagoji's RIGHT forearm, which faces the camera, has a prominent pale arrow- or feather-shaped scar. The bible puts the brand and the long white scar only on the inner LEFT forearm, and panel 2.3 on this page shows them correctly on the left arm, so the mark reads as a mirrored brand. Secondary: Padmini's horse here is a plain dark bay with no markings, almost identical to Kayal, while in 2.5 her horse has a broad white blaze.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's RIGHT forearm, the arm nearest the camera holding the reins, must be bare, smooth skin with no scar, brand, tattoo or mark of any kind. The previous image painted a pale arrow-shaped scar there, which is wrong. His only forearm marks are the brand and the long white scar on the inner LEFT forearm above the wrist. In this wide shot, keep that left forearm under the cream shoulder cloth or turned away from camera so no mark shows at all. Give Padmini's horse a broad white blaze down its face (a brown bay with a black mane and tail) so it matches her horse later on this page and cannot be mistaken for Kayal, who has no white markings. Keep everything else as it was: Nagoji and Padmini riding side by side toward the viewer at centre; the turbaned riders with tall spears at left; the Nair musketeers on foot with shouldered matchlocks and the light gun on its two-wheeled bullock-drawn carriage at right; the red dirt track and dry hills; clear open blue sky across the whole top band for lettering; Nagoji's topknot with grey at the temples, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth and white mundu, no turban, no sash; Kayal's ochre red-brown coat with black mane, tail and lower legs; Padmini's grey-threaded hair, gold necklace, cream sari hitched for riding and stick laid across her saddle.

decisions.issues: Minor: Padmini's hair reads almost all black in the dusk light, with little of the grey threading that the ch16-27 row and the neighbouring panels 2.1 and 2.5 show. Everything else matches the beat: a Kerala gatehouse with a low tiled roof and carved gable figures, cloths between trees, wall-niche oil lamps, drummers and pipers, girls carrying the flower-decked goddess palanquin, older women with brass plates, Padmini dismounted in the line with a clay lamp and her stick, and men bowing. No painted text. Clear dusk sky at top centre for the caption.

Minor: the brand patch and long white scar are correctly on Nagoji's LEFT forearm, but they sit on the outer side near the elbow rather than on the inner forearm a hand's width above the wrist, and there is an extra long pale scar on his left upper arm. Ponnan has a tiny ear stud, and his horse is the same size as Kayal rather than a head lower. These are small. Nagoji matches his sheet (topknot, grey temples, gold ear stud, clean chin, thick curled moustache, silver chain), and so does Ponnan (curly hair, no topknot, moustache, clean chin, red shoulder cloth, short jacket, spear). The tusker with its gold nettipattam and children offering bananas is present. Dusk sky across the top centre takes both balloons above the heads.

Minor: the sweet fried discs are drawn as glazed rings that look a little like pretzels, though they pass as fried festival sweets. Yusuf matches the bible (tall, lean, white skullcap, trimmed dark beard, short dark coat over a white tunic, no turban, no scar). He keeps one hand on the basket, steadies the startled boy with the other and smiles up toward someone out of frame. Same festival setting, lamps and elephant as 2.2 and 2.3. Open sky at upper left and centre takes both captions.

Page continuity: Padmini's horse has a broad white blaze and a lighter reddish coat, while in 2.1 v01 she rides a plain dark bay. The 2.1 correction asks for the blaze, so the two will match after regeneration. Otherwise this matches the beat: Padmini back at her horse with lamp-lit wall and the procession behind her, eyes bright, grey-threaded hair, gold, cream sari with gold border and her stick. No painted text, and the hands on the bridle and stick are sound. The dusk sky and trees at top centre can take her balloon clear of her face.

v01 is otherwise strong. Nagoji is mounted on a correct bay Kayal with topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, cream shoulder cloth and silver chain. Ponnan crouches with the checked cloth and coins, the cart is overturned and the shapes are under cloths, and the upper-right sky is clear for lettering. It fails the locked ear rule: Nagoji wears a hanging gold drop below the lobe, copied from the nagoji-v2 sheet, not the small flush gold stud required by CONTINUITY and the author's 2026-10-02 decision.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's ear ornament must be a small flush gold stud: one round gold bead sitting flat on the earlobe. Draw NO hanging drop, pendant, dangling bead or hoop below the lobe, and ignore the hanging drop drawn on the reference sheet. Keep everything else from this composition: Nagoji mounted on Kayal at left (bay coat, black mane and lower legs), bare-chested with the cream shoulder cloth over one shoulder, white mundu, silver chain of office, Kerala topknot with grey at the temples, thick curled moustache and clean-shaven chin, looking off toward the hills. Keep Ponnan crouched at right beside a cloth-covered body, lifting the blue-and-white checked cloth and a few silver coins. Keep the overturned grain cart with spilled paddy, the three cloth-covered shapes with no blood, and the wide open sky across the upper right left clear for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Nagoji stands dismounted, while 3.1 shows him mounted; the script does not specify either way. A faint shadow of stubble on the chin still reads as clean-shaven. The checked cloth and coins lie on the ground instead of in Ponnan's hand. A round brand and scar show on the left forearm, which the ch23 bible row allows. Otherwise the panel matches: topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, flush gold ear stud, silver chain, raided convoy setting, and a gaze toward the hills. The sky top centre and right is clear for both balloons.

The composition is right: the valley between wooded slopes, the line of spearmen and archers, plain green banners, the heavy raja small in the centre of the road, and open sky for the captions. But every matchlock man on both slopes is shown firing, with smoke puffs at the muzzles and a visible orange muzzle flash on the large lower-left gunman. That contradicts the beat: smouldering slow-match at the wrists, 'not a full ambush', 'not an attempt to kill us all'. The raja also sits on what reads as a chair with arms, not a low stool.
decisions.correction: The matchlock men on both slopes are NOT firing. Draw no muzzle smoke, no muzzle flash, and no sparks or puffs at or along any barrel; every muzzle is clean. The only smoke is a thin curl rising from the glowing coil of slow-match wound around each man's wrist. Guns are held at the ready, some levelled and some resting across knees or rocks, with no discharge. The heavy man in the exact centre of the road sits on a low, backless wooden stool, not a chair with arms or a back. Keep the rest of this composition: the full-width valley where the road dips between two wooded red-earth slopes, the line of spearmen and archers across the path, the plain unlettered green cloth banners on tall poles, the heavy bare-chested man in a white mundu with a gold-edged sash small in the centre, and the open sky across the top centre left clear for two captions.

decisions.issues: The staging is excellent: over the shoulder from behind Nagoji in the saddle, with Kayal's neck, Ponnan in red with his spear at left, the grey-haired Nair captain with a round shield at right, and the Kollamkara Raja centred on his stool with gold hoops, chains, gold-edged sash and sword. Sky is clear for three balloons. It fails the locked ear rule: Nagoji's ear, seen from behind, carries a gold hoop ring, not the small flush stud. Secondary problem: the upper-left matchlock man's muzzle shows a flame with rising smoke, which reads as a firing or burning muzzle in a no-shots standoff.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's ear ornament, seen from behind, must be a small flush gold stud on the earlobe, NOT a hoop or ring, with nothing hanging below the lobe. The matchlock men on the slopes are not firing: no flame, spark or smoke at any muzzle, only at most a thin curl of smoke from the slow-match coiled at a man's wrist. Keep everything else from this composition. In the near foreground centre: the over-the-shoulder view from behind Nagoji in the saddle, with his Kerala topknot, grey-touched long curls, bare shoulder and cream shoulder cloth, and Kayal's bay neck and bridle. At the left edge: Ponnan with curly hair, red shoulder cloth and short red jacket, and his spear. At the right edge: the older, heavier, grey-haired, grey-moustached, bare-chested Nair captain with a round shield and no chain. Beyond them, centred and facing us: the heavy Kollamkara Raja seated on his low stool with gold ear hoops, gold neck chains, white mundu, broad gold-edged waist sash and worn-hilted sword. Leave the open sky between the banners at top centre clear for three balloons.

decisions.issues: The raja is very good: heavy, bare-chested, gold ear hoops and chains, gold-edged sash and sword, hands spread, grinning, with grinning spearmen behind and wide sky for lettering. But at least four matchlock men on the upper slopes have smoke puffing from their muzzles, aimed level toward the viewer. That reads as gunfire during the parley and contradicts the standoff beat. It also clashes with 3.3 and 3.4, which are being regenerated without firing. Minor: he sits on a low chair with side posts, not a stool.
decisions.correction: The matchlock men on the upper slopes are not firing. Draw no muzzle smoke, no muzzle flash, and no puffs of smoke at or near any barrel. At most a thin curl of smoke rises from the slow-match coiled at each man's wrist, and the guns are held at the ready, not levelled to fire. The raja sits on a low, backless wooden stool, with no chair back or side posts. Keep everything else from this composition: the heavy bare-chested Kollamkara Raja centred and grinning, comfortably spreading both hands, with heavy gold ear hoops, gold neck chains, a white mundu with a broad gold-edged waist sash and a worn-hilted sword at the sash. Keep his bearded spearmen grinning behind him, the plain unlettered green banners, the red-earth valley road, and the open blue sky across the top centre left clear for three balloons.

decisions.issues: v01 gets the look right: narrowed sideways glance, heavy gold ear hoops, neck chains, gold-edged sash, plain green banners, matchlocks with smouldering match on the slopes, and no text. The framing is wrong, though. The script asks for the raja close, and v01 is a full-figure seated medium-long shot that nearly repeats the composition of 3.5. At panel size the 'eyes narrowing a fraction' beat will be unreadable. The head is about 320 px, too small to crop into a close-up at print resolution.
decisions.correction: Reframe this as a true close-up. Show the Kollamkara Raja's head and shoulders, cut at mid-chest, filling most of the frame, with his face large in the right half. Keep the expression and look from the last attempt: brows lowered, lids narrowed a fraction, eyes cut sideways toward frame left, where Nagoji sits his horse off panel. Keep his long black hair swept straight back from the brow and falling loose behind the shoulders, with no topknot or bun. Keep the thick black moustache, clean-shaven chin, heavy gold ear hoops and several gold neck chains on the bare chest. Behind him show only a soft, low-detail slice of red-earth slope with one plain faded green banner and open blue sky. Keep the upper-left third of the frame as open sky or blurred slope, with no faces or hands, for two speech balloons. Do not show his full body, the stool, his knees or feet, or the line of spearmen. This panel must not repeat the seated full-figure composition of panel 3.5.

decisions.issues: Nagoji (topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, silver chain, raised palm) and Ponnan (curly hair, red cloth, smaller horse) are good, and the foreground matchlock with its burning match works. Four problems rule it out. (1) An empty stool stands in the road behind the riders, although the raja is seated on it for the whole exchange. (2) The slope musketmen wear white with saffron and yellow turbans under yellow banners. This breaks the green-banner, indigo-head-cloth Kollamkara look of 3.3 to 3.5, 4.1 and 4.3 to 4.5, and the saffron flags risk reading as Maratha. (3) The line of men across the road wears vests and crossed belts, which muddles the geography. (4) A pink-red slash on Nagoji's left forearm reads as a fresh wound, not a pale healed brand.
decisions.correction: Keep the low angle from the slope past the foreground musketman's long Indian matchlock with its smouldering slow-match. Keep Ponnan (curly hair, moustache, red shoulder cloth, short jacket, spear, smaller horse) exactly as drawn. Keep Nagoji on Kayal exactly as drawn: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud, cream shoulder cloth over the white mundu, silver chain, open palm raised slightly, eyes not on Ponnan. Fix the valley so it matches panels 3.3 to 3.5, 4.1 and 4.5. Every Kollamkara man on the slopes, including the foreground musketman, is bare-chested or bare-shouldered with a dark indigo or earth-brown head cloth and indigo or brown cloth. None wears white clothes or a yellow or saffron turban. Every banner is plain faded green, with no yellow or saffron flag anywhere. The riders face the raja, who is off panel ahead of them toward frame right, so draw NO stool in the road. The road behind the riders shows only the Travancore column in the distance: Nair musketeers, bare-chested in white mundu with crossed leather belts, no vests, no yellow flags. Any mark on Nagoji's inner left forearm is only a faint, pale, healed patch, never a red or pink mark that could read as a fresh wound. Keep the sky at upper centre clear of flags for the two balloons.

decisions.issues: The composition works: reverse wide over the raja's bare back and gold-edged sash, Nagoji on Kayal, Nair musketeers with crossed belts, the small gun on its bullock carriage, matchlocks and green banners on both slopes, and open sky for the balloons. Nagoji's face is correct (clean chin, curled moustache, gold ear stud, topknot). Several things rule it out. (1) Nagoji is bare-chested with no cream shoulder cloth. That is a costume break from 3.1, 3.4 and 4.2 and contradicts the chapter 23 bible row (mundu with shoulder cloth). (2) From behind, the raja's hair is a curly mass with a gold-ringed topknot bun, unlike the long swept-back hair in 3.4, 3.5, 4.1, 4.4 and 4.5. (3) Nagoji points sideways at the slope rather than back the way they came. (4) A yellow flag flies in the Travancore column. (5) The mark on Nagoji's inner left forearm is dark and tattoo-like instead of a pale healed patch.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition. Keep the raja's broad bare back, gold-edged sash, gold ear hoop and wooden stool in the left foreground. Keep Nagoji on Kayal at right centre, and behind him the white-clad Nair musketeers with crossed leather belts and the small gun on its bullock carriage. Keep the matchlock men and plain green banners on both slopes and the open sky at top centre. Fix four things. First, from behind, the raja's hair must match the other panels: long, sleek black hair swept straight back from the brow and falling loose to the shoulders, with no topknot, no bun, no hair ring and no beard showing at the jaw. Second, Nagoji wears his cream shoulder cloth draped over his left shoulder and across his chest, over the white mundu, with the silver chain on top, as in panels 3.4 and 4.2. He is not bare-chested. Keep his topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin and small gold ear stud. Third, Nagoji half-turns in the saddle and gestures back over his shoulder, open hand, toward the road behind him and the column, not sideways at the slope. Any mark on his inner left forearm is only a faint, pale, healed patch, never a dark tattoo. Fourth, the Travancore column carries no yellow or saffron flag: show either no banner or a plain red standard with a silver conch and no writing.

decisions.issues: The raja's downcast eyes, ear hoops and neck chains are right. Three problems rule it out. (1) The convoy wreckage is placed in the valley right beside the raja's stool: an overturned cart, dead harnessed bullocks, barrels, a brass pot and a maroon cloth. This contradicts 3.1 and 4.3, where the convoy died on another stretch of road and Nagoji gestures back to it, and it breaks the clean road of 4.1 and 4.5. (2) The rendering drifts to a semi-photographic painted look, unlike the inked style of the rest of the page. (3) The shot is framed waist-up, not close.
decisions.correction: Remove all convoy wreckage from the valley: no cart, no fallen or dead bullocks, no barrels, sacks, pots, scattered goods or red or maroon cloth anywhere. The convoy died on a different stretch of road (panel 3.1), so the road around the raja shows the same clean red-earth road, line of bare-chested spearmen in indigo head cloths, matchlock slopes and plain faded green banners as panels 4.1 and 4.5. Frame him truly close: head and shoulders to mid-chest, face large in the right half of the frame. Keep the expression from the last attempt: eyes dropped and cut down toward frame left, as if toward the far road out of frame, mouth and jaw still slack, not yet set. Keep his long black hair swept back loose to the shoulders, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin, heavy gold ear hoops and gold neck chains. Draw it in the book's inked graphic-novel style, with clean ink line and painted colour matching panels 4.1 and 4.5, not a semi-photographic rendering. Leave the upper-left part of the frame as open sky or soft slope with no faces, for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Clean pick. The raja leans forward on the stool with a clenched scowl. His look is right: bare chest, gold ear hoops and chains, gold-edged sash, worn-hilted sword. The slopes are consistent with page 3 (matchlocks, green banners, indigo head cloths). The sepia inset with its hard border reads clearly as Colachel: palms, powder smoke, spearmen and Nairs in one line. There is no text. Minor points: one musketman at top right wears a maroon head cloth, though red is reserved for Ponnan, and the stool is plainer than the carved one in 4.1. The three balloons fit in the open sky at upper centre (x 0.25 to 0.70, y 0 to 0.2) and the low-detail hills below it. The caption sits in the inset's sky.

v01 (only candidate): the raja's carved stool sits empty in the middle of the road, but the raja is seated on it in 4.5, 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4. The Kollamkara musketmen and spearmen wear white tunics, white or dark-green turbans and green sashes under yellow banners. In 5.2 to 5.4 they are bare-chested in dark indigo with green banners. The camera sits at standing height with no horse, so Nagoji reads as on foot, but he is mounted on Kayal in 5.4. His head faces down the road toward the empty stool, not up toward the slope. His own look is fine: topknot, grey at the temples, gold ear stud, moustache, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain.
decisions.correction: Keep the over-the-shoulder composition from behind Nagoji's head and shoulder (Kerala topknot high on the crown, first grey at the temples, small gold ear stud, thick curled moustache in lost profile, cream shoulder cloth with a narrow gold border, silver chain of office) and the musketmen on both slopes with long Indian matchlocks and smouldering slow-match. Fix the following. Nagoji is MOUNTED on Kayal, so the camera sits at a rider's height just behind his head, with a sliver of Kayal's black mane and ochre red-brown neck along the bottom edge. His face is tilted clearly UP toward the musketmen on the right-hand slope, not toward the road. Every Kollamkara man matches the rest of this scene: bare-chested, dark indigo or earth-brown mundu and head cloths, no white tunics, no white turbans, no green sashes. Their banners are plain faded green and unlettered, never yellow. If the raja's stool is visible down the road, the Kollamkara Raja is seated on it (heavy, bare-chested, long wavy black hair loose to the shoulders, white mundu with a broad gold-edged waist sash, gold ear hoops and neck chains); never show an empty stool. Keep the open sky in the upper centre clear for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: v01 (only candidate): Nagoji's bare arm in the foreground carries a dark ink tattoo-like glyph that reads as a letter or symbol, plus a white scar on the outer arm. That breaks both the no-pseudo-text rule and the bible's brand (a pale puckered patch on the inner LEFT forearm, no letters). The camera faces the wrong way. We look past Nagoji's back toward the Kollamkara side, and the raja himself sits large in frame at left, so this is not the raja's point of view. The small gun is crewed by indigo-clad Kollamkara men, not Travancore musketeers, and Padmini reads as standing among Kollamkara troops. Nagoji appears on foot. In the inset the 'younger, thinner' Kollamkara still has a paunch. What works: Padmini on her horse under the tree has grey in her hair and the right sari and stick, and the warm canal-bank inset is good.
decisions.correction: Keep Padmini on her dark horse under a nearby tree (grey threading through her black hair, cream sari with gold border in the old Kerala drape, long walking stick, stern unreadable face) and the warm, soft-edged canal-bank inset in the lower right corner. Fix the following. This is the Kollamkara Raja's own point of view from his stool, so the raja must NOT appear anywhere in the frame. The camera is at his seated eye level looking up toward Nagoji, who sits mounted on Kayal (ochre red-brown bay, black mane). Only Nagoji's shoulder, cream shoulder cloth and the side of his head with the Kerala topknot show, cropped at the near frame edge, seen from the front-side, not from behind. Beyond him, down the road, is the Travancore column: Nair musketeers in white mundu with crossed leather belts and the small gun on its bullock carriage, with Padmini under the tree on their side of the road, not among the Kollamkara men. Nagoji's bare arms show no tattoo, no ink mark, no symbol, no scar and no letter-like shape; keep his forearms turned away or covered by the shoulder cloth. In the inset, the younger Kollamkara is visibly lean with no paunch, long black hair, gold ear hoops. Keep pale, low-detail sky inside the top of the inset clear for two balloons.

decisions.issues: v01 (only candidate): the Kollamkara Raja, the panel's only subject, is off-model against 4.1, 4.4, 5.2 and 5.4. Here he has a receding, balding crown with hair tied into a small topknot and a rounder, older face. In the neighbouring panels he has a full head of long wavy black hair loose to the shoulders, so he reads as a different man. The rest works: bare chest, white mundu with a gold-edged sash, gold ear hoops, layered neck chains, sword at the sash, tense shoulders, sideways glance, the indigo men, green banners, musketmen with smouldering match, and a large clear sky for the three lines.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition exactly: the Kollamkara Raja seated on his carved stool in the middle of the dusty road, shoulders hunched and tight, eyes glancing sideways. Keep his indigo-clad spearmen and archers, the plain green banners, the musketmen with smouldering slow-match on both slopes, and the wide open sky across the upper half for three balloons. Fix only his head so he matches the rest of the chapter: a full head of thick, long, wavy black hair falling loose to his shoulders, with no topknot, no bun, no receding hairline and no bald crown. He is heavy and sharp-eyed with a thick black moustache, the same face as in the neighbouring panels, with heavy gold ear hoops and layered gold neck chains. Turn his glance toward a strip of open ground at the side of the road where the two domains meet.

decisions.issues: v01 (only candidate): the composition, Kayal (correct ochre bay with black points, no white markings) and the raja (bare-chested, gold-edged sash, ear hoops, chains, sword, long wavy hair, looking up) are all good, and there is clear sky upper centre for both lines. But Nagoji is bare-chested with no cream shoulder cloth. The chapter's bible row ('cream or white mundu with shoulder cloth') and the chapter lock require it, and he wears it in 5.1, 5.2 and 5.5, so he changes costume between consecutive panels on the same page. Face, topknot, grey temples, ear stud, moustache, clean chin and silver chain are correct.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition exactly: Kayal (ochre red-brown bay with black mane, tail and lower legs, quilted ochre saddle pad) standing on the left with Nagoji mounted, and the Kollamkara Raja seated on his carved stool on the right looking up at him. Keep the indigo-clad spearmen, the plain green banners, the musketmen on the slopes and the open sky in the upper centre. Fix only Nagoji's costume to match the neighbouring panels. A cream shoulder cloth with a narrow gold border is draped over his left shoulder and across his chest, over the white mundu, with the silver chain of office visible over it. He is not bare-chested. Keep his face, Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, small gold ear stud, thick curled moustache and clean-shaven chin as they are.

decisions.issues: v01 (only candidate): Nagoji's close, level portrait is good: sheet face, thick curled moustache, essentially clean chin, gold ear stud, grey at the temples, cream shoulder cloth, and clear sky to the right for the line. Other problems: the topknot is cropped at the top edge and reads as mostly loose hair, and the silver chain is not visible. The background breaks continuity. The Kollamkara Raja, clearly readable on his stool at the centre, is slim and wears a cream jewelled turban and a white tunic, not heavy and bare-chested. His men are in white and olive tunics and turbans under yellow, white, brown and green banners, not the indigo, bare-chested troops and plain green banners of 5.2 to 5.4.
decisions.correction: Keep Nagoji's close, level, slightly upturned portrait on the left exactly as it is: the sheet face, first grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud and cream shoulder cloth with a narrow gold border. Keep the open sky to the right of his head clear for one balloon. Fix the following. Show his Kerala topknot complete, high on the crown and fully inside the frame, with the silver chain of office visible at his collar. The background must match the rest of this scene. The Kollamkara Raja on his stool is heavy and bare-chested, with long wavy black hair loose to the shoulders, no turban and no tunic or shirt, wearing a white mundu with a broad gold-edged waist sash, heavy gold ear hoops and neck chains. His men are bare-chested in dark indigo or earth-brown mundu and head cloths, with no white tunics and no turbans in yellow or white. All banners are plain faded green and unlettered, with no yellow, white or brown banners.

decisions.issues: v01 is otherwise strong. It shows the right valley road, plain green banners and the raja heaving himself up off his stool, and Nagoji is right on Kayal: topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth and a tiny gold stud on the lobe. The sky also leaves a large clear space for both balloons. It fails the bible on the brand. His LEFT forearm, the one on the reins nearest the viewer, shows its outer face, and that face carries a long white slash with a short crossbar near the elbow. At print size it reads as a cross or dagger mark. The bible puts the brand and scar on the INNER left forearm a hand's width above the wrist, as a puckered patch that is explicitly not a cross. The script for this panel does not need the brand at all.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition: the raja rising from his low stool at the centre of the road, Nagoji on Kayal at left, the spearmen, the matchlock men on both slopes, the plain green banners and the open sky above. Fix one detail. Nagoji's LEFT forearm, on the reins nearest the viewer, shows its outer face, and that outer face must be plain, unmarked skin from elbow to wrist. Draw no white line, slash, crossbar or cross-, sword- or letter-shaped mark anywhere on either arm. The old brand and the long white scar sit only on the inner face of the LEFT forearm, a hand's width above the wrist. That face is turned toward the horse's neck and is not visible in this panel. Keep the tiny flush gold stud clearly on his visible earlobe, with nothing hanging from it.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. The wide shot works: the raja waves a raised hand while his spearmen stand in two lines with the road open down the middle. The banners are plain green, there is no text and no blood, the hands are sound, and the open sky gives plenty of room for both of his balloons. One minor continuity drift: here the raja has a short dark chin beard and a small red dot on his forehead. In 5.2 to 5.4 and in 6.1 he has a moustache and stubble only. The bible sets no beard rule for him. A few spearmen also wear olive-green cloth and head cloths, where the bible asks for indigo or earth-brown.

The two riders work. Ponnan has curly hair, a moustache, the red shoulder cloth, a short jacket and a spear, and he turns toward Nagoji. Nagoji, on Kayal, has the topknot, grey temples, clean chin and silver chain. But the rest of the valley contradicts 6.1 and 6.2 and the raja's bible line. (1) A bearded, turbaned chief in a white jama and gold sash sits on a dais in the centre of the road, where the raja's stool stood. He reads as the Kollamkara Raja, but the raja is bare-chested and bare-headed and has no beard elsewhere. (2) The lining troops wear white tunics with yellow sashes, crossed belts and white turbans under bright yellow banners. In 6.1 and 6.2 they are bare-chested men in indigo with plain green banners, and the crossed belts make them read as Travancore regulars. (3) Nagoji's RIGHT wrist has a pinkish scar band. (4) Ponnan's horse is as big as Kayal, though it should be a head lower. (5) The spear points do not crowd close to the riders as the script asks.
decisions.correction: Keep the two riders as drawn: Ponnan at left with curly hair, the red shoulder cloth and a spear, leaning toward Nagoji, who rides Kayal at right with his topknot and silver chain. Change the valley to match the two previous panels. The raja's men lining both sides of the road are bare-chested spearmen in dark indigo and earth-brown cloth, with indigo or brown head cloths and round dark shields. They wear no white tunics, no yellow sashes and no crossed belts, and their spear points crowd in close on both sides of the riders. All banners are plain faded green, never yellow. Do not draw any seated, turbaned or bearded chief, dais or throne in the road. If the raja appears at all, he is small in the far distance, standing beside his low wooden stool: heavy, bare-chested and bare-headed, with loose curly hair, a moustache and no beard, in a white mundu with a gold-edged sash. Nagoji's right wrist and forearm are plain skin with no band, scar or mark. Ponnan rides a smaller Maravar horse whose head sits about a head lower than Kayal's.

decisions.issues: The core view is good: thick black smoke columns over torched pepper gardens along a canal, seen from a high ridge, with a clear grey haze for the captions. But two dead men lie in the foreground on the rocky ridge. The script has no bodies in 6.4. In 6.5 the same two men lie in the burned gardens, being covered with a cloth, so the dead appear twice in two different places and the 6.5 reveal is spent early. The raiders are not far below either: they walk a path on the near slope at the viewer's level. Several wear red head bands and one a red waist cloth, and the fallen men wear red waist cloths too, though red belongs to Ponnan alone in this chapter.
decisions.correction: Keep the high ridge viewpoint, the thick black columns of smoke over the torched pepper gardens and support poles, the canal and the wide hazy sky. Remove every fallen or lying man: there are no bodies and no dead or wounded figures anywhere in this panel. The two dead men appear only in the next panel, inside the gardens. Place the raiders far below the ridge, at the far edge of the burned gardens beyond the canal or on the far slope. They are small and unhurried as they withdraw into the scrub, in plain undyed cream or earth-brown cloth with brown or indigo head cloths. No one wears red head bands, red waist cloths or any red cloth, because red belongs to Ponnan alone in this chapter. Keep the upper band of grey haze above the smoke clear and low-detail for three captions.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Padmini matches her sheet and the chapter 16 to 27 row: cream sari with a gold border in the old Kerala drape with no blouse, gold ear studs and necklace, grey threading through her black hair, and her long walking stick gripped hard in her right hand while her left hand is clenched. The burned gardens read clearly: torched vines, cut poles and trampled red soil, with the canal at left. Two men lie still, with no wounds, and a farmer draws a cloth over one. The raiders are small on the far ridge. The dark smoke sky above and right of her head leaves room for her two balloons and the caption. Minor: the farmer wears a stitched olive short-sleeved shirt with rolled sleeves where a shoulder cloth would be more typical, and Padmini's hair sits loose and curly rather than in a clear coil at the nape.

v01 shows the ambush that belongs to 7.2: bare-chested matchlock men and archers are already firing from both banks, with a muzzle flash and powder smoke, and the camera sits behind the shooters. This gives away the surprise 'burst from cover' at the bend in 7.2 and repeats that panel. The chase itself (red rock outcrops, stream spray over mossy stones, riders in white on light horses) is right, but no branches whip at the riders' faces.
decisions.correction: This panel is the chase BEFORE the ambush. Draw no ambushers at all: no matchlocks, guns, bows, arrows, muzzle flashes or powder smoke anywhere in the frame, because the attackers first appear in the next panel. Keep the narrow track between red rock outcrops, the shallow stream over mossy stones and the hooves throwing spray. Put the camera low on the track ahead of the riders, so four or five Travancore riders in white mundu and white head cloths on light grey and cream horses gallop toward and past us in a strung-out file. They duck their heads and raise their forearms as low branches whip across their faces. No rider has a Kerala topknot with grey temples and a curled moustache, so Nagoji is not shown, and no one wears red cloth. Keep the top quarter of the frame as open sky and pale canopy with no figures or weapons, for two captions.

decisions.issues: Minor issues, acceptable. The gun locks are generic and show no slow-match, but none is clearly a flintlock or percussion lock. The grey-horse rider is falling back, hands at his chest, rather than fully thrown clear. On the cream horse, the rider's foot caught in the stirrup is readable but not emphatic. There is no blood, no text, and no lettering is needed.

Nagoji is drawn twice. The lead rider behind him at left copies his look: Kerala topknot, grey streak at the temples, thick curled moustache, white cloth with a gold-striped shoulder cloth. The rider behind that one also has a topknot and moustache. Nagoji's LEFT forearm (the rein arm) also carries a dark, inked, tattoo-like motif beside a white scar line. The bible's brand is a pale puckered patch of raised scar on the INNER forearm, never a dark design. Everything else works: Kayal is correct, head-on and filling the frame; Nagoji's face, clean chin, stud, topknot and silver chain are correct, with the talwar out; the shooter has dropped his smoking matchlock and is grabbing his sword, wide-eyed.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition exactly: Kayal head-on filling the frame through the stream spray, Nagoji with his talwar swung out to frame left, and the wide-eyed shooter at lower right who has dropped his smoking matchlock and grabs his sword hilt. Nagoji appears ONCE. The riders following behind him must not resemble him: they wear white head cloths wrapped over the whole head (no topknots, no grey at the temples), plain white shoulder cloths with no gold stripes, and short beards or no moustache. Keep them small and half hidden in spray. Both of Nagoji's forearms show plain, unmarked skin, with no tattoo, inked design, dark mark or symbol of any kind. The brand sits on the INNER side of the left forearm, turned away from the camera here. Keep a clear patch of sky at the top centre-right, free of the blade and faces, for one short caption.

decisions.issues: Acceptable, with minor issues. Ponnan matches his sheet (curly hair, moustache, clean chin, red gold-trimmed jacket and red shoulder cloth, white mundu at bare knees). His horse is a bay with a white star, distinct from Kayal. The cut stirrup strap is implied rather than shown. The tiny far body in the road has an odd leg arrangement and a red waist cloth, so it reads more like a fallen rider than the bare-chested shooter. Three ambushers at top left are still firing. The flank riders at right show their backs as well as the spear points. There is no blood, no text, and no lettering is needed.

Nagoji's LEFT forearm shows a dark, inked, tattoo-like rosette beside a pale scar line. The brand must be a pale puckered patch on the inner forearm, never a dark design (the same fault as 7.3). Ponnan's short jacket is brown here, but his sheet and the previous panel (7.4) show it deep red with gold trim, so his costume changes between adjacent panels. He also has a gold ear stud that is not on his sheet. His horse is nearly the same height as Kayal rather than a head lower. Everything else works: Nagoji's face, clean chin, stud, topknot with grey, silver chain and white mundu with shoulder cloth; Kayal is correct; both horses are wet with sweat; the regroup by the stream; and open sky at the top for three balloons.
decisions.correction: Keep this two-shot: Nagoji on Kayal at left, Ponnan breathing hard on his sweat-streaked horse at right, Travancore riders in white regrouping behind, the stream and the fallen raider at lower right, and the open sky band across the top for three balloons. Both of Nagoji's forearms show plain, unmarked skin, with no tattoo, inked rosette, dark mark or symbol. The brand sits on the INNER side of the left forearm, turned away from the camera. Ponnan wears the deep red, gold-trimmed short-sleeved jacket from his sheet and the previous panel, under his red shoulder cloth, not a brown jacket. He has no earring. His smaller Maravar horse stands a full head lower than Kayal. The soldiers in the background have lowered their muskets: the fight is over.

decisions.issues: Clean. Nagoji matches sheet and ch23 row: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, silver chain of office, cream shoulder cloth, white mundu, no turban or sash, and a pale scar line on the inner left forearm. Kayal is correct (bay, black mane, black lower legs, ochre quilted pad). Ponnan has curly hair, moustache, red shoulder cloth, short jacket, spear, bare knees, on a smaller horse. Late-afternoon ridge over thorn and rock valley, gun cart and riders behind. Minor only: one tiny background man on the right wears a red head cloth, and Ponnan seems to have a small ear stud that is not on his sheet. Open sky top right and above Ponnan takes the balloon.

Padmini herself is good: grey-threaded black hair coiled low, gold earrings and bead necklace, cream sari with gold border in the old drape, walking stick, flinty look, at the near end of the column. The problem is the mid-ground rider just ahead of her. He has long curly black hair, a moustache, a rust-red turban and a red waist sash, and rides a bay with a black mane. That is Nagoji's old commander look (ch11 to ch21). This panel's third line is NAGOJI (off), so readers will take this rider for Nagoji speaking, in a costume the ch23 lock forbids (no turban, no sash). It also breaks the chapter rule that red cloth belongs to Ponnan alone. The gun crew's orange-red sashes add to it.
decisions.correction: Keep Padmini exactly as drawn: grey-threaded black hair coiled low at the nape, gold ball earrings and gold bead necklace, cream silk sari with a narrow gold border in the old Kerala drape with no blouse, long wooden walking stick in her right hand, flinty sideways look. Keep her on her brown horse at the near, rear end of the column, with the ridge, the thorn-and-rock valley, the gun with its white oxen and the late-afternoon sky. Change everyone else in the column: every turban or head cloth is plain white or undyed cotton, and every waist sash is white, undyed or plain brown. Put no red, rust, orange or maroon turban, sash or cloth anywhere in the panel, because red cloth belongs to Ponnan alone in this chapter. Draw no rider with long curly hair, a thick moustache and a turban on a bay horse with a black mane, because that reads as Nagoji's old commander look. Nagoji is off-panel to the right at the head of the column, so leave the sky to the right of Padmini's head open and low-detail.

decisions.issues: Anachronism in the key action. The gun captain presses his eye to a telescopic sight, a scope with an eyepiece, mounted on a boxy breech block, and holds it like binoculars. Gunners of the 1740s sighted by eye along a plain muzzle-loading barrel. Everything else works: Nagoji matches (topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth, white mundu, beside the gun), the bare-chested crew in white head cloths haul on ropes, and the ridge, sky and lettering space are good.
decisions.correction: Keep Nagoji exactly as drawn, standing beside the gun with one hand on his hip: topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth, white mundu. Keep the sweating bare-chested crew in white head cloths hauling the carriage on ropes, the rocky ridge, the thorn valley and the late-afternoon sky. Fix the gun and the gun captain. The gun is a plain 1740s muzzle-loading bronze or iron field gun on a two-wheeled wooden carriage: smooth barrel, a rounded cascabel knob at the rear, a touch-hole on top, no breech block, no box or mechanism at the rear and no sight of any kind. The gun captain crouches behind the breech and sights with his naked eye along the top of the bare barrel toward the thickest scrub, one eye closed, one hand on the carriage trail or the wooden elevating wedge. Nothing is held to his eye: no telescope, scope, tube, binoculars or optical device anywhere in the panel.

decisions.issues: The beat itself is good: wide view, muzzle flame, a great bank of smoke, birds bursting from the trees, open sky for the caption. The gun crew is the problem. Every man wears a rust-red or orange turban, a red waist sash, a brown waistcoat and a long shirt. The large kneeling man in the foreground wears exactly Nagoji's old commander colours (rust-red turban with a red sash). That breaks the ch23 rule that red cloth belongs to Ponnan alone, and the bible bars that combination on others so they never read as Nagoji, who stood beside this gun one panel earlier. The same crew was bare-chested in white head cloths in 8.3, so the costume also jumps between neighbouring panels. Smaller point: the gunner leans over the barrel at the moment it fires.
decisions.correction: Keep the composition: the wide view from behind and beside the gun on the rocky ridge, the bright muzzle flame, the great bank of white smoke rolling out over the thorn valley, the burst of dark birds exploding out of the trees across the valley, and the open late-afternoon sky above. Change the gun crew to match the previous panel: sweating bare-chested men in white mundu with plain white cotton head cloths, no waistcoats, no long shirts, no turbans. Put no red, rust, orange or maroon turban, sash or cloth on anyone. A rust-red turban with a red sash is Nagoji's old commander look, and red cloth belongs to Ponnan alone in this chapter. The gun is a plain muzzle-loading field gun on a two-wheeled wooden carriage. The gunner stands clear to one side of the carriage and touches a linstock to the touch-hole at arm's length, not leaning over the barrel. The white draught oxen stay back behind the gun.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Nagoji matches sheet and ch23 row: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth, white mundu, no turban or sash. He is on foot with his talwar drawn, leading spearmen down off the ridge into the thorn, with the gun and riders left on the crest. Hands and sword grip are sound. Minor: a small rider top left wears a rust-red turban, and the small spearman at lower right wears a red head cloth. Both are against the chapter's red-for-Ponnan rule, but they are distant, and Nagoji is unmistakably the foreground figure. Open sky top right takes both the 'Now.' balloon and the caption.

v01 is strong on almost everything: Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch23 row (Kerala topknot tied high, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, silver chain, cream gold-bordered shoulder cloth, white mundu), thorns catch at the cloth, and the matchlock ball tears the leaves beside his ear with the gunman visible behind. The single blocker is the brand on his braced LEFT forearm. It is painted as a dark red-brown glyph that reads like a 'Z' or a '4' (pseudo-text, a letter or numeral), next to a white scar line. The bible requires a pale puckered patch with no legible letters or numerals, and the script does not call for the brand in this beat. Minor: the background raider's head cloth is rust-orange, close to the old commander-turban colour. Earth-brown would be safer.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition, lighting and figure: Nagoji crouched in the thorn, head turned toward the shot, topknot tied high on the crown with grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, silver chain, cream gold-bordered shoulder cloth over the LEFT shoulder, white mundu, his hand braced on the rock, the matchlock ball shredding the leaves beside his ear and the gunman half-hidden behind a boulder in the smoke. Change only his arms: turn the braced LEFT forearm so its inner side faces away from the camera, so the visible skin of both forearms is plain and unmarked. No brand, no scar line, no dark or red marks, and no letter-like or number-like shapes anywhere on his skin. Give the background gunman a plain earth-brown or indigo head cloth, not rust-red or orange.

decisions.issues: v01 fails the character lock. Nagoji has loose shoulder-length curly hair with no topknot and no grey at the temples. He wears a cream wrap tunic with sleeves instead of being bare-chested under the cream shoulder cloth seen in 9.1 and 9.4. A red band shows at his waist, against the NO red sash rule, and there is no silver chain. The beat is also weak: the spearman is not lunging from behind a bush at close range, the point passes in front of his belly rather than scraping past his hip, and his elbow is held level a body-length away from the man's jaw instead of driving up into it. Bodies, a dropped spear and a shield already lie in the background, which pre-empts the 9.4 aftermath reveal.
decisions.correction: Nagoji must match 9.1 exactly: Kerala topknot tied high on the crown, first grey at the temples, the hair at the sides pulled up rather than hanging loose, bare-chested under a cream gold-bordered shoulder cloth worn over the LEFT shoulder, white mundu with NO red or coloured waistband or sash, silver chain of office on his bare chest, small gold ear stud, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin. No tunic and no sleeves. Stage it tight and close, within arm's reach: a bare-chested raider in an earth-brown head cloth bursts out from behind a thorn bush and thrusts a spear, Nagoji twists sideways so the spearhead slides just past his hip, and his bent arm is already swinging upward so the point of his elbow is a hand's width under the raider's jaw. Freeze the instant before contact: no hit, no blood. Keep the same dim green-brown thorn setting as 9.1. No bodies, dropped weapons or shields in the background.

decisions.issues: v01 fails the character lock and the staging. Nagoji has loose curly hair with no topknot, no grey at the temples and no silver chain. Neither figure is a silhouette: both are fully lit in daylight, against the script's two dark figures in front of a bright wall of powder smoke with only a rim light on the raider's ash-smeared face. Nagoji stands a stride away with his sword held low behind him, not stepping inside the raised swing. The background dagger man slipping on loose stones and the ash-smeared raider face did work and should be kept.
decisions.correction: Make both foreground figures true dark silhouettes, near-black and flat, set against a bright, pale, glowing wall of grey-white powder smoke that fills the background. The only light is a low warm rim light from the side that catches the raider's face, so the grey ash smeared across his cheeks and brow reads clearly while his body stays dark. The raider holds his curved sword raised high overhead. Nagoji has already stepped inside the swing, close against the raider's chest under the raised arm. His silhouette profile must clearly show the Kerala topknot tied high on the crown (no loose hair hanging to the shoulders), the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, the shoulder cloth and the mundu. Keep the smaller background figure as in the previous attempt: a raider with a dagger in his fist, slipping and off-balance on loose stones. No contact, no blood, and the same thorn and rock valley as the rest of the page.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Nagoji matches the lock: hair gathered into a topknot on the crown, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin (soot specks only), small gold ear stud, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth over the LEFT shoulder (consistent with 9.1). He is drawn chest-up and close with soot and sweat. The three raiders lie still behind him with no wounds: the spearman left, the swordsman centre, the dagger man right. Minor points: (1) the topknot is looser than in 9.1, with more hair hanging at the sides; (2) the dead raiders are rendered sharp rather than in soft focus; (3) the left spearman's spear butt disappears behind his head (it reads as planted in the ground, not as a wound, but the letterer could check it at print size); (4) the shoulder cloth here is plain white, without the gold border seen in 9.1. For the two captions, the top-right corner over the cliff and smoke (about x 0.66 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.20) is clear and covers no face or key action. The top-left thorn corner is a second option.

The boy himself is right: thin, beardless, about sixteen or younger, small hair knot, torn brown shoulder cloth, pressed against a rock face, empty hands raised open with sound fingers, terrified eyes. The panel fails on who is present and on period. Three extra armed men surround him: a gunman, a spearman and a swordsman with cross-belts at the right edge. The script stages the boy alone, cornered by Nagoji off-panel, and page 10 has only Nagoji and Ponnan with him. The right swordsman could be misread as Nagoji in the wrong costume. The left man's gun is also anachronistic: a later rifle with steel barrel bands, a sling swivel, a trigger guard and a capped muzzle, not a 1740s Indian matchlock.
decisions.correction: Keep the boy exactly as drawn: thin and beardless, about sixteen, hair in a small knot, torn brown shoulder cloth, a torn white mundu, crouched with his back pressed against the pale rock face, both empty hands raised palms-out, eyes wide with terror looking up toward the viewer. Show NO other people in the frame, living or dead: no raiders, no soldiers, no partial figures at the edges, and no guns, spears or swords pointing at him. The threat is the viewer's position: the camera is at the eye level of an unseen man standing over him, looking slightly down. At most, the edge of one dark standing shadow falls across the stones at his feet from the bottom of the frame. Same thorn scrub, rocks and late-afternoon smoke-hazed light as the rest of the page. Leave the plain rock face above and to the right of his head clear and low in detail for a speech balloon.

decisions.issues: v01 gets Nagoji's face right: topknot, grey temples, gold stud, curled moustache, clean chin, silver chain, soot, white mundu and cream shoulder cloth, teeth bared. But the old brand on his forearm (centre right) is painted as a dark stamped circle with a glyph inside. That reads as an emblem or pseudo-letter, not the bible's pale puckered patch of ridges. He also sits relaxed on the ground with his arm on his knee and no talwar, which breaks the beat: he is standing over the cornered boy, and 10.2 to 10.4 show him upright with the blade. Two living armed men watch from the left and right edges (one with a matchlock, one with a spear), which muddies the scene after the three raiders were shown dead in 9.4.
decisions.correction: Show Nagoji STANDING, chest-up and close, leaning slightly forward toward the cornered boy off-panel, his right fist gripping the talwar hilt at the bottom edge of the frame, the blade out of frame. Keep exactly what worked: Kerala topknot high on the crown, first grey at the temples, small gold ear stud, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, silver chain of office, bare soot-streaked chest, white mundu with cream shoulder cloth, thorn branches and drifting powder smoke against pale cliffs. Make the laugh uglier: head tipped back, teeth bared, eyes narrowed and cruel, not cheerful. Keep his LEFT forearm out of frame or turned away so no brand shows. If any brand is visible, it is only a pale puckered patch of raised ridges, never a dark ring, emblem, glyph or letter. No other living person in the frame, only the still bodies lying in soft focus behind him. Leave the upper right sky and smoke clear for a caption and a speech balloon.

decisions.issues: The framing works: low angle from behind the boy, talwar raised two-handed against a white sky, thorn and rock, open sky for the caption. But Nagoji is off-model for chapter 23. He has no topknot (long loose hair), no grey at the temples and no silver chain, and he wears a long-sleeved cream tunic with a brown-red waist sash and a scabbard, not the bare-chested white mundu and cream shoulder cloth of 10.1 and 10.4. His face is calm, not the ugly bloodlust of the beat. The boy has shaggy loose hair and a torn tunic, not the small hair knot and torn brown shoulder cloth he has in 9.5.
decisions.correction: Keep the low angle from behind the boy's head and shoulders, the talwar raised high two-handed against a white sky, and the thorn, rocks and smoke. Redraw Nagoji in his chapter 23 look, matching 10.1: Kerala topknot high on the crown, first grey at the temples, small gold ear stud, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, silver chain of office on a BARE soot-streaked chest, white mundu with a cream shoulder cloth over one shoulder. NO tunic, NO sleeves, NO waist sash of any colour, NO scabbard. His face is twisted in an ugly, eager snarl. The boy in the foreground is thin and beardless, about sixteen, hair in a small knot, a torn brown shoulder cloth, shrinking down with his empty hands raised. Keep the upper sky clear for the caption.

decisions.issues: This is not the tight arm-only insert the script calls for. It is a wide two-shot with both faces drawn, and both men are mounted on horses, though the fight in the thorn is on foot. Nagoji wears a long cream tunic with a leather belt, not the bare-chested mundu look of 10.1 and 10.4. The boy and the overhead strike from 10.2 are lost. Dead bodies are also laid prominently across the midground of an insert that should be only hands and blade.
decisions.correction: Make this a TIGHT INSERT, on foot, with no horses and no faces. Show only Nagoji's bare, soot-streaked forearm and fist gripping the talwar hilt, the blade angled up against the white sky as in 10.2. From the RIGHT edge of the frame, Ponnan's hand clamps hard around Nagoji's wrist just above the hilt, knuckles tight. Only Ponnan's forearm shows, with the edge of his short deep-red jacket sleeve with gold trim and a fold of red shoulder cloth at the frame edge. No tunic sleeve on Nagoji. The blade is frozen mid-stroke. Background: thorn branches and pale smoke-hazed sky only, no bodies and no people. Keep a clear patch of sky in the upper left for an off-panel speech balloon.

decisions.issues: Both men are on-model. Nagoji has topknot, grey, gold stud, curled moustache, clean chin, silver chain and white mundu with shoulder cloth. Ponnan has curly hair, a soot-streaked face, the red shoulder cloth and a short jacket, and he grips Nagoji's scarred forearm. But Nagoji holds TWO talwars: one raised freely overhead in his right hand at top left, and a second hilt below where Ponnan grips. That breaks the beat ('the blade stops'). The tangle of hands around the lower hilt also makes it unclear who holds that sword. Ponnan's jacket is cream here but red on his sheet.
decisions.correction: Keep the composition, the thorn setting, Nagoji's chapter 23 look and Ponnan's soot-streaked face and grip. Nagoji holds ONLY ONE talwar, in the hand whose wrist Ponnan is gripping, and that blade is being forced down toward the ground. His OTHER hand is EMPTY: a bare fist cocked back at shoulder height as he spins, ready to strike whoever grabbed him, with NO second sword anywhere in the frame. Ponnan grips Nagoji's sword wrist with both hands, every finger clearly his, and Nagoji's own fist stays wrapped around the single hilt below them. Ponnan wears his sheet look: curly hair, no topknot, thick moustache, clean chin, short deep-red jacket with gold-edged short sleeves, red shoulder cloth, white mundu hitched to the knee. Keep the open sky in the upper right clear for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Ponnan is on-model (curly hair, moustache, clean chin, red jacket and shoulder cloth) and grips Nagoji's wrist with his mouth open. But this is a medium two-shot, not the close shot on Ponnan the script calls for. Nagoji sits on the ground instead of standing as in 10.4. The gripped hand is an empty fist, so the talwar has vanished between panels. Nagoji has no silver chain of office, which the chapter 23 bible row requires. Two living armed men walk through the background with matchlocks, which pulls focus from the confrontation.
decisions.correction: Make this a CLOSE shot on Ponnan, chest-up, filling the left two-thirds of the frame. He stands upright, face streaked with soot, eyes clear and hard, mouth open mid-word. Keep his look: curly hair, no topknot, thick moustache, clean chin, short deep-red jacket with gold-edged short sleeves, red shoulder cloth. His fist still clamps Nagoji's wrist in the lower foreground, and Nagoji's hand still grips the single talwar hilt with the blade pointing DOWN. Nagoji stands at the right edge, partly cropped, NOT seated: topknot, grey at the temples, small gold ear stud, curled moustache, clean chin, the silver chain of office on his bare soot-streaked chest, cream shoulder cloth over a white mundu. Background: thorn and pale powder smoke only, with no other living figures. Keep the upper area of smoke and sky clear for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only: the chain of office is a heavy coin-and-medallion chain here but a thin beaded chain in 11.4. The brand on the inner left forearm is a small dark circular mark rather than a pale puckered patch, though it has no letters and no cross. The dead raiders lying nearby are a heavier aftermath than the script asks for, but there is no blood. Nagoji matches his sheet and the chapter 23 row (topknot, grey at the temples, gold stud, curled moustache, clean chin, white mundu and shoulder cloth, dark dulled talwar). The boy sobs against the rock. The pale sky at the top centre and top right takes the caption and Nagoji's line without covering his face or the blade.

Nagoji does not have the chapter 23 look. His long curly hair hangs loose with no Kerala topknot and no grey at the temples. There is no silver chain of office, and the earrings do not match (a dangling ring in one ear, a stud in the other). The beat is also wrong. The bearded raider gripping the boy's shoulder cloth stands fully visible in the centre, while Nagoji swings his talwar at a second raider cut off by the right border. The script has one raider: the boy's captor, cut off by the right border, is the man Nagoji strikes.
decisions.correction: Nagoji must wear the chapter 23 Ananthan Pillai look exactly as in panels 11.1 and 11.4: his long curly black hair gathered into a Kerala topknot high on the crown (never loose on the shoulders, no turban), first grey at the temples, one small gold ear stud in each visible ear (no dangling rings), thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, the silver chain of office on his bare chest, white mundu with the cream shoulder cloth, no sash. Draw only ONE raider in the foreground: the bearded older raider in a head cloth, bare-chested, standing at the far RIGHT with most of his body cut off by the right panel border. His arm reaches left and his fist is knotted in the shoulder cloth of the boy, who twists free and runs LEFT, fully visible and untouched. Nagoji steps in just right of centre, between the boy and that raider, and his talwar arcs at that same raider, never toward the boy. No second raider being struck. Keep the thorn scrub, the drifting smoke, the rocky slope and the boy's ragged cream shoulder cloth and dhoti from this version.

decisions.issues: Nagoji is in the wrong costume, so he does not match the chapter 23 row or panels 11.1 and 11.4. His curly hair hangs loose down his back with no topknot, and he wears a long-sleeved cream tunic and loose trousers (the commander cut without the turban) instead of a bare-armed white mundu and shoulder cloth. The rest works: the boy runs into the thorn, cloth-covered bodies lie on the rocks with no blood, and the talwar hangs at Nagoji's side with his back to us.
decisions.correction: Nagoji, seen from behind in the foreground, must wear the chapter 23 Ananthan Pillai dress exactly as in panel 11.1: his long curly black hair gathered into a Kerala topknot high on the crown, with first grey at the temples (never loose curls down the back, no turban). His back and arms are bare, with the cream shoulder cloth draped over one shoulder and a white ankle-length mundu wrapped at the waist. No long-sleeved tunic, no trousers, no sash. The silver chain of office shows at the side of his neck, and a small gold ear stud is visible. The talwar hangs down at his side in his right hand, its blade dulled dark, never red. Keep the composition: the boy small in the mid-ground, feet slipping on rock as he disappears into the thorn scrub; cloth-covered bodies and dropped spears and matchlocks on the rocks, no blood; drifting smoke and a rock face behind.

decisions.issues: Minor only: a thin dull orange-brown waistband shows under the mundu fold at Nagoji's waist. It is not a broad red sash, but it is worth a glance. His chain of office is a thin beaded chain rather than the heavier chain in 11.1. Padmini's bay has a small white star on its forehead, a detail the bible does not fix. The beat is correct: a sunset ridge, rows of cloth-covered bodies dragged into lines on the valley floor, and Padmini on her horse with grey threading her coiled hair, cream sari with gold border, gold jewellery. Nagoji climbs up on foot (topknot, grey, stud, moustache, clean chin, silver chain), his mundu and forearms soaked to the elbows in dark brown stains, never red. The wide sunset sky across the top takes all four lettering lines.

Minor only: at 6x zoom, the gold border on Ponnan's sleeve breaks into faint capital-letter-like glyphs. At the frame's own size and at print size they read as ornamental pattern, but they could be smoothed in retouch. A small background bullock driver by the gun carriage wears a red head cloth, against the rule that red cloth is Ponnan's alone this chapter. The light gun on its bullock carriage matches the chapter's column (2.1, 4.3). The beat is correct: Ponnan (curly hair, no topknot, heavy moustache, red shoulder cloth over a short red jacket, white mundu) wipes his spear with a cloth, and Padmini turns her horse away, looking back over her shoulder (grey in her coiled hair, cream sari with gold border, walking stick). It is the same sunset ridge as 11.4. The open sky above both heads takes the two speech lines.

Acceptable with minor drift. The hall matches the script: laterite walls, carved teak ceiling, grey stone floor, brass lamps and a tall doorway at the far end. Ramayyan matches his sheet at the low desk, with the palm-leaf strips fanned, the cord loose and the stylus in hand. Nagoji has a topknot, grey temples, gold stud, curled moustache, silver chain, mundu and shoulder cloth, and stands stiffly with his hands clasped. The scar is correctly on his LEFT forearm. Padmini has her chin high and her stick. Minor points: Varma has a grey temple streak and a gold stud earring, so he reads close to Nagoji (he wears pearl drops in 12.2). His hair knot sits at the back of his head, not above the left ear. He stands in thought rather than pacing. Nagoji's chin has faint stubble shading. There is no text. Lettering: the caption goes top-left over the ceiling, Ramayyan's balloon over the wall and window left of Varma, and Nagoji's over the ceiling above the doorway.

Varma in the foreground is good: he turns with a cold sidelong glare, and has pearl drops, gold beads and cream-and-gold cloth. But the man at the low desk in the background is not Ramayyan. He is a second Varma: a grey-streaked topknot, a thick curled moustache, the same red-and-white forehead mark, a gold chain and a bare chest. It reads as a duplicate king, or a Nagoji double, in Ramayyan's seat, and it breaks continuity with 12.1, 12.3 and 12.5.
decisions.correction: Varma must be the only person in the frame. In the last attempt, the man at the low desk in the background was drawn as a second Varma (grey-streaked topknot, thick curled moustache, forehead mark, gold chain, bare chest) instead of Ramayyan, and he reads as a duplicate king. Keep Varma exactly as drawn in the foreground: turning back over his shoulder with a cold sidelong glare, grey-flecked black hair gathered in a side knot above his LEFT ear, no turban and no crest, pearl drop earrings, gold bead necklaces, a cream-and-gold cloth over one shoulder, bare chest, and a cream mundu with a gold border. Keep the same pillared hall: laterite walls, carved teak ceiling, grey stone floor, brass oil lamps and the tall doorway at the far end. Remove the desk and any seated or standing figure. Frame Varma from the knees up in the left half of the panel, with pillars, wall and the doorway filling the right half. Leave plain laterite wall or ceiling above and to the right of his head clear for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Clean. Padmini (grey threading in her hair, gold necklace and stud earrings, cream sari with gold border, stick) cuts in with an open hand. Ramayyan matches his sheet, seated at the low desk and snapping back with the stylus pointed. The hands are sound. It is the same hall, with the same lamps and doorway, as 12.1. There is no text. Lettering space: Padmini's balloon over the ceiling and pillars between the two heads; Ramayyan's two balloons over the ceiling and wall above his head at upper right.

Nagoji in the foreground matches his sheet and bible row, and the sepia, hard-bordered inset of the boy's raised hands against the rock in the lower right corner is right. But the man writing at the low desk in the background is not Ramayyan. He has a grey topknot, a thick curled moustache and a silver chain, so he reads as a second, older Nagoji. Also, the brand on Nagoji's LEFT forearm is drawn as a dark, tattoo-like glyph rather than a pale ridged patch, and the flush in his neck barely shows.
decisions.correction: Nagoji must be the only person in the hall. In the last attempt, the man at the low desk in the background had a grey topknot, a thick moustache and a silver chain, so he read as a second, older Nagoji rather than Ramayyan. Keep Nagoji exactly as drawn in the left foreground: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, small gold ear stud, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, silver chain of office, white mundu and cream shoulder cloth, fists clenched at his sides, gaze turned toward the right edge. Keep the small sepia inset in the lower right corner, with its hard border, showing the boy's two raised hands against the rock face. Show no desk and no other figure: the background is the empty pillared hall, with the laterite wall, brass oil lamps and the tall doorway at the far end. Add a visible dull red flush creeping up the side of his neck. On his inner LEFT forearm, the old brand is a pale puckered patch of raised ridges beside a thin white scar, never a dark tattoo-like mark. Keep plain laterite wall clear at the upper right, away from his face, for two balloons (Varma speaks from off panel to the right).

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Nagoji kneels on the floor with his head bowed, rather than standing and bowing his head. It is a stronger submission than the script asks for, but it carries the beat. His look matches: topknot, grey temples, gold stud, curled moustache, silver chain, scar on the LEFT forearm. The brand is only a small dark smudge, barely visible. Ramayyan is unmoved at the desk and matches his sheet. Padmini's head is turning sharply toward the right. She is in frame, so her '(off)' line's tail point is set at her own mouth. It is the same hall as 12.1 and 12.3. There is no text. Lettering space: Nagoji's balloon goes top-left over the pillars, Padmini's over the ceiling or doorway sky near her head, and Ramayyan's over the wall above him at upper right.

Minor only: Varma has no namam on his brow here (he wears one in 12.2 and 13.2) and his knot sits at the back of the head rather than clearly above the left ear. Nagoji matches the bible: topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud, silver chain, faint marks on the LEFT forearm. Ramayyan and Padmini (grey threading through her hair) match their sheets. The ceiling band and the space above the doorway are clear for both Padmini balloons.

An extra man sits at Ramayyan's desk with the palm-leaf bundle and stylus, but he is off-model: an older man with a namam, rudraksha beads, a red-bordered cloth, a thick moustache and a topknot. Readers will take him for Ramayyan, and he does not match the Ramayyan sheet (thin, clean-shaven, receding hair with curly sides, plain white cloth). The panel's cast is Varma alone. Varma's open-palm gesture is also aimed at this man instead of at Padmini, whom his line addresses ('Amma').
decisions.correction: Show Varma ALONE in the frame: no other person anywhere, no seated scribe, no man at a low desk, no palm-leaf bundles or desk in view (Ramayyan and Padmini are off-panel). Medium shot of Varma from the knees up, seated on the low cushioned seat of the previous panel and leaning slightly forward, his body and gaze turned toward frame LEFT, where Padmini stands off-panel. One open palm is lowered toward her in a calm, conciliatory gesture, and his face is quiet and not unkind, brows relaxed. Keep his look exactly as drawn in v01: V13 face, Vaishnavite namam on the brow, thick curled moustache, clean chin, bare-headed with his hair in a side knot above his LEFT ear, no turban, no crest, bare-chested, gold bead necklaces, cream mundu with a gold border and a gold-bordered cloth over his left shoulder. Same laterite-walled audience hall with carved teak pillars, brass lamps and a grey stone floor. Keep the upper third of the frame, above and to the left of his head, as plain wall or ceiling so a long speech balloon can sit there without touching his face or hand.

decisions.issues: A young man with a topknot, thick moustache and gold pendant sits writing at Ramayyan's desk in the background. He reads either as a wrong Ramayyan (who is thin, clean-shaven, with receding curly hair) or as a Nagoji double at the wrong place. The panel's cast is Padmini alone, so this figure is off-model. Padmini herself is good: grey-threaded hair coiled at the nape, gold border sari, stick, and a disgusted look.
decisions.correction: Show Padmini ALONE in the frame: no other person anywhere, no seated scribe or man at a desk in the background, no partial figure or chair back in the foreground; the king and Nagoji are off-panel. Waist-up or three-quarter shot of Padmini standing with her long walking stick in her RIGHT hand. Her head is turned and her eyes cut sideways toward the off-panel men at frame LEFT, lips pressed and nostrils flared, a look of disgust that could be aimed at them or at him.
