Keep her look exactly as drawn in v01: grey threading through thick black hair coiled at the nape, gold ear studs and a gold necklace, cream silk sari with a narrow gold border in the old Kerala drape with no stitched blouse. Same audience hall behind her: laterite walls, carved teak pillars, brass lamps, grey stone floor and the tall doorway at the far end. Keep the upper part of the frame on the side she faces as plain wall or ceiling for two speech balloons, clear of her face and hands.

decisions.issues: Framing deviation: the script asks for the three men 'small in the hall'. Here Varma (left, gold beads) and Nagoji (right, seen from behind) are large foreground figures, with Padmini small in the doorway. The beat still reads: Padmini's back going out through the tall doorway, her stick planted on the grey stone, Ramayyan correct at his desk, and the three men left behind watching. Nagoji's brand and scar show on the back of his LEFT forearm in this rear view, with no letters and no cross. This is a silent panel, so no lettering space is needed.

Ramayyan has three hands. His right hand holds the stylus, his left hand is raised in the wave, and a third hand cups the palm-leaf bundle from below with no arm attached. Everything else works: Ramayyan looks down at the leaf, and Nagoji, on-model, bows with joined palms, turning to go. The hall matches the rest of the page, and there is clear space above Ramayyan for his lines.
decisions.correction: Ramayyan must have exactly TWO arms and two hands. His RIGHT hand holds the iron stylus, resting on palm-leaf strips that lie flat and open on the desk in front of him. His LEFT hand is lifted loosely from the wrist in a small dismissive wave. No hand holds the bundle from below, there is no third hand anywhere, and his eyes stay down on the leaf. Keep everything else as drawn in v01. Ramayyan: thin face, receding hair with curly sides, plain white cloth. Nagoji at frame right: Kerala topknot with grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, silver chain of office, white mundu with a cream shoulder cloth, no turban, no sash. He bows low with palms joined at his chest, one foot stepping toward frame right as he turns to go. Same laterite audience hall with carved teak pillars, brass lamps, grey stone floor and the tall doorway at the far end. Keep plain wall and ceiling space above Ramayyan's head for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor, acceptable: the shoulder cloth is still draped over his right shoulder rather than set aside (a folded striped cloth on the side table partly covers the beat). The left-forearm brand is drawn near the elbow as a small concentric-ring mark with a pinkish scar line, not a pale puckered patch a hand's width above the wrist (no letters or cross). The chain-of-office medallion has tiny notches around its rim that read as ornament, not legible script. Light stubble shading on the jaw, which reads as shading at print size. Beat, lamp, topknot with grey at the temples, gold ear stud, raw red knuckles and faintly pink water all work. Captions fit the plain dark wall at upper left or upper centre.

Minor, acceptable: the knuckles are no longer visibly raw. The left forearm shows a brown blotch and a pale oval near the wrist, with the white scar running across the arm instead of along it. A faint white line also appears on the right forearm. Padmini has a tiny dark dot between her brows that is not on her sheet. The doorway is on the left here and on the right in 14.1, which can read as the reverse angle of the same room. Beat, shawl, still walking stick, topknot, chain and ear stud are all correct. The plain wall between the figures (and the night sky in the doorway) gives room for all three balloons.

v01: Nagoji wears no silver chain of office, though the chapter 23 bible row requires it and 14.1 and 14.2 show it. The brand on his inner left forearm is a crisp drawn circle with a line through it, like a phi or null sign, so it reads as a pseudo-letter and not as a pale puckered patch. Padmini has lost the shawl she wore pulled tight in 14.2 (and that 14.5 calls for). Composition, lamp between them, faces and the wall space for lettering are good.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition exactly: Padmini stepping in through the doorway at left, leaning forward on her long walking stick, frowning; Nagoji seated cross-legged on the woven mat at right, looking up at her; the clay lamp on its stool and the brass basin on the floor between them; the plain laterite wall above. Fixes: Nagoji wears his silver chain of office around his neck, lying on his bare chest, the same chain as in the previous panel. Padmini wears the same fawn woollen shawl from the previous panel around her shoulders over her cream sari, loosened now as she steps in. The brand on Nagoji's inner LEFT forearm is only a faint, irregular pale patch of puckered raised scar tissue a hand's width above the wrist, blurred and organic, beside the long thin white scar. Do not draw a circle, a line through a circle, any symbol, glyph, letter, numeral, cross or geometric shape there; if in doubt, turn that forearm so the brand is not seen.

decisions.issues: v01: the brand on Nagoji's left forearm is a dark letter-like glyph (like a capital A with a bar over it), which counts as painted pseudo-text and breaks the bible's pale puckered patch. Nagoji wears no silver chain of office (required by the ch23 row and shown in 14.1 and 14.2). Padmini's shawl from 14.2 is missing. The lamp sits on the floor below and between them rather than between their faces. The whisper pose, faces, ear stud, moustache, Padmini's grey threading and the wall space for two balloons all work.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition: Padmini kneeling close at left, leaning in with one hand cupped beside her mouth as she whispers, her long walking stick upright in her other hand; Nagoji seated cross-legged at right in profile, turned to her, listening; the plain laterite wall above their heads and the doorway at right. Fixes: Nagoji wears his silver chain of office around his neck, lying on his bare chest, as in the earlier panels on this page. Padmini wears the same fawn woollen shawl from the earlier panel around her shoulders over her cream sari, loosened. Set the small clay oil lamp on a low wooden stool between them so its flame sits between and just below their two faces, lighting both. The brand on Nagoji's inner LEFT forearm is only a faint, irregular pale patch of puckered raised scar tissue a hand's width above the wrist, blurred and organic, beside the long thin white scar. Do not draw any dark tattoo-like mark, glyph, symbol, letter, numeral, cross or geometric shape on either arm.

decisions.issues: Acceptable with logged deviations. The over-the-shoulder view of open, scrubbed hands works, with sound anatomy (thumbs on the correct sides, five digits each). The brand is on the LEFT wrist as scripted, but it is a crisp dark square stamp with a hollow centre, not a pale puckered patch. It has no letters or cross. White scar lines appear on both wrists, so the right wrist carries a scar the bible reserves for the left arm. The faint pale line across the LEFT palm is not distinct. Ridged nails cannot be seen palms-up; the fingertips show dark purple bruising instead, which reads as old injury, not gore. Padmini is crouched, clutching the end of her cream sari at one bare shoulder rather than straightening with the 14.2 shawl slipping. If 14.3 and 14.4 are regenerated with the shawl, this will read as the shawl gone. Lettering fits the wall above the lamp and basin and the dark mass of Nagoji's hair at upper left (for the caption).

v01 (only candidate): Marthanda Varma is drawn as a near-twin of Nagoji. He has the same crown topknot, the same grey streak at the temple, the same small gold ear stud, the same thick curled moustache and a red dot on the brow, so the reader cannot tell the King from his escort commander. The bible and script call for the V13 varma-v1 face with the temple-scene side knot above his LEFT ear, his pearl drop earrings and sandal paste on the brow. Nagoji (left, silver chain) has a red forehead dot, which the bible forbids ('No forehead marks'). He also stands in the front rank at the King's side instead of at the outer perimeter among the spearmen. What works: the gopuram, belikal stones, caparisoned elephants, crowd, hard sky and the heir (sheet-accurate face, white namam, thin gold chain, small white mundu, top bun).
decisions.correction: Keep the gopuram, the belikal offering stones, the caparisoned elephants, the crowd, the hard blue sky and the heir exactly as drawn. Marthanda Varma must not resemble Nagoji: give him the V13 varma-v1 face (longer, narrower face, slightly hooded eyes, a neater moustache curled at the tips), jet-black hair with NO grey streak, worn in a side knot above his LEFT ear (never a crown topknot), pearl drop earrings (never a small gold stud), a pale sandal-paste line on the brow (no red dot), bare-chested, a white silk angavastram with a gold border over one shoulder, gold necklaces and heavy rings on both hands; he stands in the centre foreground with the boy beside him. Nagoji is smaller, in the middle ground at the outer edge of the scene among the white-clad spearmen, a few paces behind and to one side of the royal pair and clearly apart from them: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, white mundu, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, and NO forehead mark or red dot. Give Nagoji no gold necklace and give Varma no silver chain. Leave open sky across the top left for two captions.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. The beat is clear: a lean, bare-chested devotee in a plain white mundu with close-cropped hair and three ash lines slips low out of the front of the crowd past the white-clad escort, with the gopuram and elephants behind. Minor points: (1) at full zoom there is a faint thin shadow on his upper lip that could be read as a pencil moustache (the script says NO moustache), but it is barely visible at panel size; (2) the rendering is more painterly than the inked style of 15.1 and 15.4; (3) the escort here wears white turbans, white tunics and leather cross-belts, which should be the reference for 15.3. The open sky at the top centre (x about 0.35 to 0.6, y about 0.03 to 0.2) takes the caption without covering anything.

v01 (only candidate): the leaping devotee has a clearly drawn dark moustache, while the script states 'no moustache' for 15.2, 15.3 and 16.1. His mundu now has red border stripes, unlike the plain white mundu in 15.2. The escort has also changed from 15.2: head cloths, red waist sashes, no cross-belts. Both foreground spearmen hold their spear points angled away from the attacker. What works: the leap over the line of spears, the curved gutting knife, close-cropped hair, ash lines, the belikal stones, the brass lamps, the gopuram, and open sky top left and centre for captions.
decisions.correction: Keep the leap over the line of spears, the curved gutting knife in his right hand, the gopuram, the belikal stones, the brass lamps and the open sky exactly as drawn. The leaping devotee must be completely clean-shaven: NO moustache, no pencil line and no stubble on the upper lip, a bare upper lip and chin, hair cropped close, three pale ash lines across the brow. His mundu is plain white with NO red border, matching panel 15.2. The escort spearmen match 15.2: white turbans, white sleeveless tunics with dark leather cross-belts, white mundus, no red sashes. Their spear points are raised and angled up toward the man flying over them, not pointing away from him. Keep the sky clear above and to the left of the leaping figure for two captions.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. The heir matches his sheet: sharp cheekbones, wide frightened eyes, white namam, thin gold chain, small white mundu. He is frozen on the flagstones with one hand raised as the curved knife comes down at him from the upper right, with the gopuram, elephants and escort behind. Minor points: (1) his hair is a loose curly mass rather than the sheet's neat topknot (the topknot is only required for chapters 17 and 22); (2) his crossed ankles are slightly ambiguous, with one foot hidden; (3) the attacker's mundu has a red border like 15.3, and the background spearmen are bare-chested rather than in the white tunics of 15.2. The inked style matches 15.1. There is caption space in the sky between the gopuram top and the knife (x about 0.36 to 0.54, y about 0.03 to 0.2), or on the flagstones at bottom left.

v01 (only candidate) misses the beat and breaks continuity. (1) Varma crouches facing the viewer and looks right instead of throwing his body across the heir with his BACK and LEFT shoulder turned to the falling blade. (2) The blade does not fall: it is a broad, sword-like blade held level at head height. The attacker wears black, gold-trimmed sleeves, whereas the chaver is bare-chested in a white mundu. (3) Varma again copies Nagoji's look: crown topknot, grey temple streak, gold ear stud.
